scratch.text: A job's own exit code from `gcloud run jobs execute --wait` is not proof of success -- the wrapping shell/tool exit code and the underlying gcloud command's own stdout must both be checked. Twice this session, a background task notification reported 'completed (exit code 0)' for an execution that had actually printed 'ERROR: (gcloud.run.jobs.execute) The execution failed.' to its own output. Always tail the actual output, never trust the notification summary alone.

A COUNT(*) or GROUP BY aggregate query against a table that just received a large bulk write can be dramatically slower than its own EXPLAIN cost estimate suggests (timed out repeatedly at 15-60s across many attempts before one 80s attempt finally returned) -- likely visibility-map/heap-fetch overhead before autovacuum catches up. A LIMIT-bounded sample query remains fast throughout and is a reliable interim verification signal; don't conclude a write failed just because an aggregate count times out.
